q: Does BRSR require a board sustainability committee?
title: BRSR and a board sustainability committee
short: No. BRSR does not make a board sustainability committee mandatory. It asks you to name the highest authority responsible for your business responsibility policies and to answer Yes or No on whether a board committee or director is responsible for sustainability decisions, with details if Yes. A No is allowed, but investors will see it.

sections.h: The governance questions in BRSR Section B
ul: Question 8: details of the highest authority responsible for implementing and overseeing the business responsibility policies.
Question 9: whether the company has a specified committee of the board, or a director, responsible for decision making on sustainability issues. Yes or No, with details if Yes.
Question 10: how the company reviews its performance against the nine NGRBC principles, whether that review is done by a director, a board committee or another committee, and how often.

p: Regulation 34(2)(f) of the SEBI LODR Regulations requires the top 1,000 listed entities by market capitalisation to include a BRSR in their annual report. Other listed companies may file one voluntarily. Unlisted companies are not covered, though they may receive value chain questions from listed customers.

sections.h: Board rules that do touch sustainability
ul: Risk management committee: LODR Regulation 21 requires one for the top 1,000 listed entities, and its role in Schedule II includes identifying sustainability risks, in particular ESG related risks.
CSR committee under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013: it oversees CSR policy and spending. It is not a sustainability committee unless its charter says so.
A dedicated ESG or sustainability committee of the board, with its own charter.
An existing committee, often risk management or CSR, whose charter has been widened to cover sustainability decisions.
A named director given responsibility for sustainability.
No committee, with the highest authority and review frequency disclosed under Questions 8 and 10.
p: Whichever applies, answer from what the board charter and minutes support, because investors and assurance providers may ask to see them.
